title: Human Evolution Lineage & Cranial Capacities
topic: Dryopithecus to Homo sapiens, Brain Sizes (cc), Tools, Fire, & Cave Art
quickSummary: Chronological human evolution: Dryopithecus (~15 mya, ape-like) -> Ramapithecus (~15 mya, man-like) -> Australopithecus (3-4 mya, 400-500 cc, upright bipedal, fruit eater) -> Homo habilis (2-1.5 mya, 650-800 cc, first toolmaker, no meat) -> Homo erectus (1.5 mya, 900 cc, meat eater, first to use fire) -> Neanderthal Man (100-40 kya, 1400 cc, burial rituals) -> Homo sapiens (75-10 kya, 1350-1450 cc, cave art 18 kya, agriculture 10 kya).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Human evolution proceeded from Dryopithecus/Ramapithecus through Australopithecus (bipedal, 400-500 cc), Homo habilis (tool-maker, non-meat eater, 650-800 cc), Homo erectus (meat eater, used fire, 900 cc), Neanderthals (burial ceremonies, 1400 cc), to modern Homo sapiens (1350-1450 cc, cave art 18 kya, agriculture 10 kya).

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 10.1 Comprehensive Hominid Evolutionary Matrix

| Hominid Ancestor | Geological Age | Cranial Capacity | Key Locomotor & Cultural Traits | Significant Fossils |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ***Dryopithecus*** | $\approx 15\text{ mya}$ (Miocene) | Not determined | Arboreal; ape-like; hairy; arms & legs equal length | Africa and Europe |
| ***Ramapithecus*** | $\approx 15\text{ mya}$ (Miocene) | Not determined | More man-like; semi-erect posture; parabolic dental arch | Shivalik Hills, India (*Edward Lewis*) |
| ***Australopithecus*** | $\approx 3\text{--}4\text{ mya}$ (Pliocene) | **$400\text{--}500\text{ cc}$** | **Upright bipedal gait**; lived in African grasslands; fruit eater | "Lucy" (*Ethiopia*); *Taung Child* |
| ***Homo habilis*** | $\approx 2.0\text{--}1.5\text{ mya}$ | **$650\text{--}800\text{ cc}$** | First hominid / **"Handy Man"**; crafted stone tools; **did NOT eat meat** | Olduvai Gorge, Tanzania (*Leakey*) |
| ***Homo erectus*** | $\approx 1.5\text{ mya}$ (Pleistocene) | **$900\text{ cc}$** | Fully erect posture; **ate meat**; **first to use fire** | Java Man (*H. e. erectus*); Peking Man |
| ***Homo neanderthalensis*** | $100,000\text{--}40,000\text{ ya}$ | **$1400\text{ cc}$** | Heavy brow ridges; robust build; **buried dead with rituals**; animal hides | Neander Valley, Germany |
| ***Homo sapiens*** | $75,000\text{--}10,000\text{ ya}$ | **$1350\text{--}1450\text{ cc}$** | Modern human; arose in Africa; cave art ($\approx 18,000\text{ ya}$ Bhimbetka); agriculture ($\approx 10,000\text{ ya}$) | Cro-Magnon Man $\rightarrow$ Modern Humans |

conceptBreakdown.heading: Bipedalism vs Encephalization
conceptBreakdown.title: Bipedalism vs Encephalization
conceptBreakdown.content: Fossil evidence from Australopithecus proves that upright bipedal locomotion evolved millions of years before significant encephalization (brain volume enlargement).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Out of Africa vs Multiregional Hypothesis
conceptBreakdown.title: Out of Africa vs Multiregional Hypothesis
conceptBreakdown.content: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and Y-chromosome sequencing strongly support the Recent African Origin ('Out of Africa') model, indicating modern Homo sapiens arose in Africa ~200,000 years ago and migrated across Eurasia.
